strengths: Novel problem formulation identifying visual-interactive capabilities as an important but overlooked modality for embedding models
High-quality benchmark construction: SCaR with 1M samples, sophisticated negative generation (3 types), multi-stage filtering, high inter-annotator agreement (κ=0.89), and diverse source datasets
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: extensive ablations (9 dimensions), robustness analysis (jitter/masking/offset), prompt type analysis, and multiple operational mode comparisons
Consistent and substantial improvements on visual-interactive tasks (6.3-20.3% on SCaR), with reasonable gains on MMEB across all meta-tasks
Impressive stability on catastrophic forgetting: VIRTUE maintains MMEB performance when finetuned on SCaR while other baselines show severe degradation (19.8-59 point drops)
Strong reproducibility support: code/models/benchmark to be released, detailed implementation documentation, and clear data collection procedures with prompt templates
Practical demonstrations of real-world applications: visual-interactive I2I retrieval and on-the-fly correction with visual hinting
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core approach straightforwardly combines SAM2 with VLM via simple concatenation; segmentation-language connector is just Conv2D + 2 MLPs (Eq. 1)
Modest improvements on main MMEB benchmark: only +2.0 points for 7B model (66.6→68.6), raising questions about whether added computational complexity is justified for non-interactive scenarios

Concerning dependency on uniform point sampling: removing uniform points drops MMEB by 3.1 points (Table 5), suggesting model becomes dependent on segmentation rather than learning universally better representations

Limited scope of visual-interactive evaluation: SCaR only evaluates image-to-text with bounding boxes; interactive image-to-image retrieval relegated to appendix case studies due to copyright/ethical concerns

Unfair SCaR comparisons: VIRTUE natively handles visual prompts while baselines adapted through text descriptions, making it difficult to isolate benefits; other baselines not originally designed for this task
Computational overhead not well justified: +82ms inference latency (5x slower) and +1.1GB memory with modest MMEB improvements; cost-benefit analysis missing

SCaR quality concerns: 11% sample dropout, synthetic caption generation via GPT-4V for ADE20K, element-swapping negatives may not reflect real challenging cases, and three-element structure somewhat artificial
Missing statistical significance testing: no confidence intervals or significance tests despite claiming consistent improvements across benchmarks
Limited failure analysis: insufficient discussion of when VIRTUE underperforms, which object/scene types benefit most from visual interaction, or scenarios where visual prompts hurt performance
